I found no runtime import cycle among the files in `packages/core/injector`. I worked this out by reading imports and checking how each imported name is used. I didn't run a tool like madge, because I didn't want to install one.

**Why there is no cycle:** `Module` is the name most likely to close a loop, and it is used only as a type everywhere except `container.ts`. A type-only use is erased when TypeScript compiles, so it doesn't count as a runtime import. The same holds for the other back-edges: `ContextId` in `constants.ts`, and `NestContainer` in `module.ts` and `module-ref.ts`. The tsconfig doesn't turn on `verbatimModuleSyntax` or `importsNotUsedAsValues`, so these imports really are dropped.

The runtime edges that remain all point one way:
- `container` → `module` → `module-ref` → `injector` → `instance-wrapper` → `constants`
- `module-ref` → `abstract-instance-resolver`
- `module-ref` → `instance-links-host`
- `injector` → `inquirer` and `settlement-signal`
- `container` → `compiler`, `modules-container`, `internal-core-module` and the opaque-key factories
- `internal-core-module-factory` → `container`, `injector`, `instance-loader` and `lazy-module-loader`
- `lazy-module-loader` → `instance-loader`

Nothing points back up the chain. Without the type-only exclusion, you would see cycles between `module`, `container`, `instance-wrapper`, `module-ref`, `injector` and `constants`.

- I didn't trace edges that leave the folder, such as `scanner`, `services` and `router`. A cycle could pass through one of those.

**Only `ClientKafka` (`client-kafka.ts`) is part of a cycle in the source, and it isn't a runtime cycle.**

The cycle is a source-level one between `client/client-kafka.ts` and `helpers/kafka-reply-partition-assigner.ts`:

- `client-kafka.ts` imports `KafkaReplyPartitionAssigner` from `../helpers`. It uses it as a value, so this import stays in the compiled output.
- `kafka-reply-partition-assigner.ts` imports `ClientKafka` from `../client/client-kafka`. It uses it only as a constructor parameter type (`private readonly clientKafka: ClientKafka`). The class has no decorators, so the import isn't needed at runtime. I found no `importsNotUsedAsValues`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` or `preserveValueImports` settings in the tsconfigs, so TypeScript drops that import when it compiles. I haven't built the package to confirm this in the emitted JS.

So `ClientKafka` forms an import cycle in the source, but the compiled JS should have no cycle.

I ruled out the others:

- **`ClientGrpcProxy`, `ClientMqtt`, `ClientNats`, `ClientRedis`, `ClientRMQ` and `ClientTCP`:** they import only `./client-proxy` plus leaf modules (`constants`, `errors`, `events`, `serializers`, `helpers`). None of those lead back to the client files at runtime.
- **`interfaces/client-metadata.interface.ts` and `interfaces/client-kafka-proxy.interface.ts`:** both import `ClientProxy` from `../client`, and `client-proxy.ts` imports from `../interfaces`. They use `ClientProxy` only in type positions (`Type<ClientProxy>`, `extends ClientProxy<…>`), so those imports are also dropped when compiled.
- **`ClientProxyFactory`:** it imports every client, but nothing the clients import leads back to it.

I read the imports with grep rather than running a tool like madge, so this is based on reading the code.

Eight client implementations in `packages/microservices/client` are in a runtime import cycle (reported as `typeOnly: false`), along with the client factory and base class. They sit in one 29-file group, and the tool reports every cycle in the repo as runtime:

- `client-grpc.ts`
- `client-kafka.ts`
- `client-mqtt.ts`
- `client-nats.ts`
- `client-redis.ts`
- `client-rmq.ts`
- `client-tcp.ts`
- `client-proxy.ts` (the base class)
- `client-proxy-factory.ts`
- `client/index.ts` (the barrel file)

The tool lists only the members of the group and one shortest loop through it, not every loop. The loop it reports is:

`client-grpc.ts` → `interfaces/index.ts` → `interfaces/client-kafka-proxy.interface.ts` → `client/index.ts` → `client-grpc.ts`

The barrel files cause this. The `interfaces` barrel pulls in `client-kafka-proxy.interface.ts`, which imports from `client/index.ts`. That barrel re-exports every client, so each client that imports from `interfaces` gets pulled into the loop.
